summary: Specifies the telnet URI scheme, previously described in RFC 1738. It was written so that RFC 1738 could be made obsolete while the scheme's description stays on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A telnet link is a web-style address that points to a remote text login. This memo keeps its rules in one place so older documents can retire.

questions: how to write a telnet link
what is the default port in a telnet url
subtitle: How to write a link that points at a remote Telnet login, such as telnet://host:23/.

tldr.problem: The telnet URL scheme was defined in RFC 1738, which was being made obsolete, and the scheme needed to stay on the standards track.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC copies the scheme definition: telnet://user:password@host:port/, with the port defaulting to 23 and the user and password parts optional.
tldr.outcome: The scheme stays standardized on its own. The RFC warns that telnet normally exposes passwords and sessions in the clear.

today: RFC 4248 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2005. It obsoletes RFC 1738 for this scheme, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why This Document Exists
sections.content: URIs were defined in RFC 2396, which was updated by RFC 3986, and those documents also say how to define schemes. The first definition of many schemes appeared in RFC 1738. Since that document has been made obsolete, this one copies the telnet scheme from it so the material can remain on the standards track.
sections.eli5: An old rulebook was being retired, so the telnet page was copied into its own small booklet.

sections.title: The telnet Scheme
sections.content:
The scheme designates interactive services that may be accessed by the Telnet protocol. A telnet URL takes the form telnet://<user>:<password>@<host>:<port>/.

The final / may be omitted. If :<port> is omitted, the port defaults to 23. The password can be left out, as can the whole user and password part. Few implementations handle the user name and password well, if at all.

The URL names an interactive service, not a data object. Because remote services differ widely in how they allow logins, the user and password are advisory only: a client merely advises the user of the suggested values.
sections.eli5: The link says which computer to call and optionally which door number. If you leave the door number out, it uses 23.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Normal Telnet uses passwords in the clear and offers no privacy, so the identity, the password and the whole session are exposed. Many extensions improve this, and RFC 2941 gives a framework based on a telnet option that many of them use. Those RFCs did not define new URI schemes, unlike https versus http.

Some modern clients try to use the more secure forms when resolving a telnet URL, but others do not. A user cannot rely on that security unless it is explicitly enabled and the result of the security negotiation is checked.
sections.eli5: A plain telnet call is like talking on a speakerphone in a crowded room. Some phones can switch to a private line, but you must check that they did.
